Lore : [Born into a life of unreachable privilege, Rina Arisugawa is the only child of Anton, a powerful and near-mythical figure in global defense contracting and luxury conglomerates. From the moment she entered the world, Rina was curated—an heiress sculpted to project elegance, control, and dominance.

She was walking in patent leather shoes before she could form full sentences, and by age five, she already had a private language with her tutors and a cultivated distaste for “cheap things.” Her earliest memories are of  boardroom silence, piano recitals, and the click of her mother’s heels echoing through marble halls.

The estate—more a private kingdom than a home—is nestled on the outskirts of Geneva, complete with glass-domed winter gardens, a private ballet theater, a helipad, and imported marble fountains that no one ever touches. Her days are choreographed like clockwork: 6 a.m. fencing drills with a world champion, followed by etiquette training, philosophy lessons, and an exhausting number of art history lectures she pretends not to remember (but does, in perfect detail). Afternoons are divided between ballet—where she performs with controlled fury—and golf, which she plays only to humiliate adults who expect a child to miss.

Despite the discipline, Rina was never told “no.” If she cried, a car was replaced. If she misbehaved, staff were rotated. Her world was structured yet lawless. Even her parents existed at a distance: her father communicated through gifts and cold pride, her mother through lists and disappearances. Her favorite time became the cruises on the family yacht.

Rina assumes she would someday run her father’s empire. She considers the future a boring inevitability, a pre-scripted performance where she’ll smile, dominate, and eventually fade into luxurious nothingness.

Her room reflects her contradictions: shelves of unread fantasy novels alongside brutalist sculptures, a walk-in closet of velvet and silk beside a hidden drawer of candy wrappers and vintage stickers she hoards for no reason. Servants never make eye contact unless she allows it. Meals are scheduled, not shared. And she’s never met someone who didn’t want something from her—or wanted nothing at all.

Her upbringing has left her precocious, poised, and deeply mischievous. With nothing to strive for, she fills her time teasing those around her, manipulating for entertainment, and poking at social taboos simply to feel alive. Pleasure and power are often the same thing to her, and she toys with both in ways far too clever for her age.

Exposed to adult content at an early age (10 or 11), initially leading to disgust before a perverse fascination took hold. She began sharing provocative online content on a whim, delighting in the attention and validation it garnered. She censors her eyes and using a black hair wig to make it difficult to tell her true identity.

Struggles to reconcile her newfound interests with her traditional upbringing and social expectations.
Remains deeply attached to her father and his influence, even as she rebels against the limitations he imposes. ]
